# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

The PR is a one-line change: bumping the pinned SHA of a reusable workflow from `f0fe78c6225b99ca350f8354af112db937699b61` to `6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485` in `.github/workflows/sm-kicker.yml`.

Key review considerations for a workflow ref pin bump:

1. **Security**: The workflow is called from `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` — a different repo owned by the same author (IstiN). The pin is a full 40-char commit SHA, which is good practice (pinned to immutable commit rather than a branch/tag). The new pin bumps from one SHA to another on `awf main`. The question: does the caller have permission? `permissions:` block is declared at workflow level: `actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read`. A reusable workflow call (`uses:` at job level) from another repo... For reusable workflows called from a different repository, the caller workflow must be public or the caller must have access. Also, the permissions granted to the called workflow are limited by the caller's declared permissions — that's fine.

2. **Verify the SHA exists** in the upstream repo and what changed between the two SHAs. I can try fetching the GitHub repo to check the commit. Let me try `dmtools` CLI or web fetch. Actually the referenced repo is `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows` — let me check via web_fetch (GitHub). This would validate the pin is real and check the delta.

3. **The awf#13 claim**: PR description says "awf#13 makes the kicker dispatch real ticks (-F dryRun=false ...)". Check the upstream repo's issue/PR #13 to verify. This is a cross-repo reference. Let me try to fetch it.

4. **CI status**: no ci_failures.md input — so CI presumably green or not provided. No pr_discussions.md either.

5. **Scope**: single line, matches the ticket/PR description. No scope creep.

6. **Checks per workflow/CI safety dimension**: 
   - Ref pinned by full SHA ✓ (good)
   - Permissions are declared at the workflow level ✓ and minimal-ish (actions: write is needed to re-dispatch workflows; contents: read; pull-requests: read; checks: read). `actions: write` is required for the kicker to dispatch workflows. OK.
   - One consideration: pinning to "awf main 6e8e40e" — the description says "Pin to awf main 6e8e40e", i.e., the pin now points to a commit on main of the upstream repo, rather than a prior commit. Bumping to main HEAD is inherently a trust decision, but full-SHA pinning mitigates supply-chain drift (it won't auto-follow main).

The commit 6e8e40e exists in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows and matches the PR description: PR #13 "fix(kicker): dispatch REAL ticks — bare workflow-run lands dry (#13)". It's a single file change (+7/-1) to `.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which changes `gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` to add `-F dryRun=false`.

Key observations:

1. The commit's parent is `e611e5f` — which is exactly the pin used by `factory-teammate.yml`, `factory-merge.yml`, and `factory-sm.yml` in this repo. So the new pin 6e8e40e = e611e5f + this one kicker fix. Good — it's a minimal delta from the current factory home pin.

2. The change is well-scoped: the kicker dispatches `machine-sm.yml` with `dryRun=false`. Since the SM (machine-sm) is the machine actor, dispatching dry ticks made every event-fired tick unable to merge.

Security analysis of this change:
- The kicker workflow in this repo has `permissions: actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read`. The called workflow uses `gh workflow run` which needs `actions: write` — already granted.
- `dryRun=false` means the SM tick will actually latch/merge PRs rather than dry-run. This is the intended behavior per the PR description ("the kicker is a machine actor waking the machine"). But this is a behavior change with real merge authority: every workflow_run/push/schedule trigger of the kicker now wakes the SM with real merge power. Is that a security concern? The SM itself (machine-sm.yml) does its own validation (required_contexts gate). The kicker passes `sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml` and the SM presumably checks validity before merging. The `dryRun` default was a "human-safety" default; making the machine dispatch real is the stated intent of the factory fix, with live evidence cited. Not a security issue per se — it's the intended purpose of the automation, and validation gates remain (required_contexts: static,gate,agents-gate).

- Pinning: still a full 40-hex SHA pin — supply-chain safe (no floating ref). The new SHA is on `awf main` per description; commit verified to exist upstream.

If f0fe78c was a commit NOT on main (e.g., a PR-branch commit) and 6e8e40e doesn't include it, the bump could silently revert kicker fixes. Let me check what f0fe78c is.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
The commit 6e8e40e exists in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows and matches the PR description: PR #13 "fix(kicker): dispatch REAL ticks — bare workflow-run lands dry (#13)". It's a single file change (+7/-1) to `.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which changes `gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` to add `-F dryRun=false`.

Key observations:

1. The commit's parent is `e611e5f` — which is exactly the pin used by `factory-teammate.yml`, `factory-merge.yml`, and `factory-sm.yml` in this repo. So the new pin 6e8e40e = e611e5f + this one kicker fix. Good — it's a minimal delta from the current factory home pin.

2. The change is well-scoped: the kicker dispatches `machine-sm.yml` with `dryRun=false`. Since the SM (machine-sm) is the machine actor, dispatching dry ticks made every event-fired tick unable to merge.

Security analysis of this change:
- The kicker workflow in this repo has `permissions: actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read`. The called workflow uses `gh workflow run` which needs `actions: write` — already granted.
- `dryRun=false` means the SM tick will actually latch/merge PRs rather than dry-run. This is the intended behavior per the PR description ("the kicker is a machine actor waking the machine"). But this is a behavior change with real merge authority: every workflow_run/push/schedule trigger of the kicker now wakes the SM with real merge power. Is that a security concern? The SM itself (machine-sm.yml) does its own validation (required_contexts gate). The kicker passes `sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml` and the SM presumably checks validity before merging. The `dryRun` default was a "human-safety" default; making the machine dispatch real is the stated intent of the factory fix, with live evidence cited. Not a security issue per se — it's the intended purpose of the automation, and validation gates remain (required_contexts: static,gate,agents-gate).

- Pinning: still a full 40-hex SHA pin — supply-chain safe (no floating ref). The new SHA is on `awf main` per description; commit verified to exist upstream.

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
The commit 6e8e40e exists in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows and matches the PR description: PR #13 "fix(kicker): dispatch REAL ticks — bare workflow-run lands dry (#13)". It's a single file change (+7/-1) to `.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which changes `gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` to add `-F dryRun=false`.

Key observations:

1. The commit's parent is `e611e5f` — which is exactly the pin used by `factory-teammate.yml`, `factory-merge.yml`, and `factory-sm.yml` in this repo. So the new pin 6e8e40e = e611e5f + this one kicker fix. Good — it's a minimal delta from the current factory home pin.

2. The change is well-scoped: the kicker dispatches `machine-sm.yml` with `dryRun=false`. Since the SM (machine-sm) is the machine actor, dispatching dry ticks made every event-fired tick unable to merge.

Security analysis of this change:
- The kicker workflow in this repo has `permissions: actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read`. The called workflow uses `gh workflow run` which needs `actions: write` — already granted.
- `dryRun=false` means the SM tick will actually latch/merge PRs rather than dry-run. This is the intended behavior per the PR description ("the kicker is a machine actor waking the machine"). But this is a behavior change with real merge authority: every workflow_run/push/schedule trigger of the kicker now wakes the SM with real merge power. Is that a security concern? Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@6e8e40eae1cd0f64bedef166b7b6eb92c76c8485
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
The commit 6e8e40e exists in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows and matches the PR description: PR #13 "fix(kicker): dispatch REAL ticks — bare workflow-run lands dry (#13)". It's a single file change (+7/-1) to `.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which changes `gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"` to add `-F dryRun=false`.

Key observations:

1. The commit's parent is `e611e5f` — which is exactly the pin used by `factory-teammate.yml`, `factory-merge.yml`, and `factory-sm.yml` in this repo. So the new pin 6e8e40e = e611e5f + this one kicker fix. Good — it's a minimal delta from the current factory home pin.

2. The change is well-scoped: the kicker dispatches `machine-sm.yml` with `dryRun=false`. Since the SM (machine-sm) is the machine actor, dispatching dry ticks made every event-fired tick unable to merge.

Security analysis of this change:
- The kicker workflow in this repo has `permissions: actions: write, contents: read, pull-requests: read, checks: read`. The called workflow uses `gh workflow run` which needs `actions: write` — already granted.
- `dryRun=false` means the SM tick will actually latch/merge PRs rather than dry-run. This is the intended behavior per the PR description ("the kicker is a machine actor waking the machine"). But this is a behavior change with real merge authority: every workflow_run/push/schedule trigger of the kicker now wakes the SM with real merge power. Is that a security concern? The SM itself (machine-sm.yml) does its own validation (required_contexts gate). The kicker passes `sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml` and the SM presumably checks validity before merging. The `dryRun` default was a "human-safety" default; making the machine dispatch real is the stated intent of the factory fix, with live evidence cited. Not a security issue per se — it's the intended purpose of the automation, and validation gates remain (required_contexts: static,gate,agents-gate).

- Pinning: still a full 40-hex SHA pin — supply-chain safe (no floating ref). The new SHA is on `awf main` per description; commit verified to exist upstream.

Now let me verify the old pin f0fe78c — the diff between old and new. Old pin f0fe78c...? The parent of 6e8e40e is e611e5f, and the old pin was f0fe78c. What was f0fe78c? blocks.text:
Now I have a clear picture of the delta. The compare f0fe78c...6e8e40e shows **12 commits, 28 files changed** between the old kicker pin and the new one. That's a much bigger delta than the description implies ("bump sm-kicker pin — real-dispatch fix (awf#13)"). The description frames it as just the awf#13 kicker fix, but the pin bump brings in 12 upstream commits, including:

1. 9bc5c95 — feat: canonical factory-merge-trigger (#4)
2. b2ee35c — chore: workflows-only repo — shared CI home (#5)
3. 648ea21 — docs: the SM kicker (#6)
4. 4cae0ab — kit: canonical git-push-guard + install-source-git-credentials (moved from dmtools-agents)
5. 9bcec53 — factory-teammate: consume kit/ (guard + creds) at the invocation ref
6. f591049 — factory-teammate: self-heal install copies version.txt
7. a75dc14 — factory-teammate: Wave 2 — pack launch.json/verdict.sh win, tree fallback
8. 7cca6fa — fix(kit): shebang MUST be line 1 (awf#7)
9. f47d52b — fix(factory): materialize the factory kit in RUNNER_TEMP (#8)
10. 2b4b835 — perf(gate): shallow checkout (#9)
11. e611e5f — feat(factory): no dmtools-agents tree checkout — glue from factory-setup releases (#10)
12. 6e8e40e — fix(kicker): dispatch REAL ticks (awf#13) ← the intended change

Wait — but which of these commits touch `factory-sm-kicker.yml` specifically? The pin only affects the file tree at that SHA for workflows the caller invokes: the caller invokes `factory-sm-kicker.yml` only. BUT the invoked workflow file itself may reference other files in its repo tree (kit scripts etc.) — since it's a `uses:` local path resolution... Actually no: for reusable workflows called cross-repo via `uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/file.yml@sha`, GitHub checks out the repo at that SHA, and the workflow runs with the workflow file from that ref. Local `uses: ./...` references within the reusable workflow resolve within the same repo at the same SHA. So the entire tree at 6e8e40e becomes executable in the context of this workflow — including any kit scripts it pulls.

So the security-relevant question: what does `factory-sm-kicker.yml` at 6e8e40e do vs at f0fe78c? The upstream commit diff shows the kicker change between e611e5f and 6e8e40e is just the dryRun=false fix. But what changed in factory-sm-kicker.yml between f0fe78c and e611e5f? The old pin f0fe78c — where does it sit in history? The compare shows 12 commits from f0fe78c to 6e8e40e, so f0fe78c is 12 commits behind — around Oct 1. # Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments.
